name: Cartagena
tagline: A UNESCO-listed walled Spanish colonial city on the Caribbean, all bougainvillea balconies, salsa in the plazas, sunset on the ramparts and island beaches a boat ride away.
highlight: Watching the sun set from the old city walls with a cold drink as the plazas fill with music.
shortDescription: A colourful walled port city with the Clock Tower, San Felipe fortress, Getsemaní's street art, Caribbean seafood, nightlife and boat trips to the Rosario Islands.
metaDescription: A Cartagena travel guide: the walled city, Clock Tower, Castillo San Felipe de Barajas, Getsemaní, Rosario Islands, seafood, salsa, where to stay, safety and a three-day plan.
knownFor: Colonial old town, Caribbean beaches, seafood, nightlife

image.file: File:Colombia, Cartagena, Sector Antiguo, Plaza de Santo Domingo.jpg
image.alt: Plaza de Santo Domingo in the old city of Cartagena with coloured colonial buildings

intro: Cartagena de Indias was founded by the Spanish in 1533, and for two centuries it was the main port through which the wealth of the Americas, including gold and emeralds, was shipped to Spain. Pirates and privateers, including Sir Francis Drake, attacked it repeatedly, and in response the Spanish built miles of stone walls and forts that survive today. The walled city and its fortresses are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

Inside the walls, the old town is a maze of cobbled streets, plazas and coloured houses with wooden balconies draped in bougainvillea. Sidewalk cafés, fruit vendors, palenqueras in bright dresses and horse-drawn carriages give it a theatrical air, and in the evening the plazas fill with music. Just outside the walls, Getsemaní, once a working-class quarter, is now a lively neighbourhood of street art, hostels and bars.

Cartagena is hot and humid, so days are best spent early or on the water. The Castillo San Felipe de Barajas fortress is the largest built by the Spanish in the Americas, and boats take visitors to the Rosario Islands for snorkelling and beaches. Three or four days is a good stay, and the city is a natural start or end to a Colombian trip.

whyVisit.intro: Cartagena is one of the most beautiful and atmospheric colonial cities in the Americas.

attractionsIntro: The old city is compact and best on foot, with the fortress and islands as excursions.

attractions.name: The Clock Tower and the walled city

image.alt: The yellow Clock Tower gateway at the entrance to Cartagena's walled city

attractions.text: The Torre del Reloj is the main gate into the walled city, opening onto the Plaza de los Coches and a maze of colonial streets.

attractions.name: Castillo San Felipe de Barajas

image.file: File:Castillo San Felipe de Barajas, Cartagena 15.jpg
image.alt: The stone walls of Castillo San Felipe de Barajas above Cartagena

attractions.text: The largest Spanish fortress in the Americas, built in the 17th century on a hill with tunnels and cannon.
attractions.tip: Go early, since it is hot.

attractions.name: The walls and sunset

image.file: File:Bocagrande skyline from Baluarte San Francisco Javier CTG 11 2019 2158.jpg
image.alt: The Bocagrande skyline seen from the old city ramparts

attractions.text: The ramparts around the old city make a lovely walk, with a sunset drinking spot at Café del Mar.

attractions.name: Rosario Islands

image.file: File:Cocolise Isla Resort, Islas del Rosario (23938753124).jpg
image.alt: A resort on the turquoise waters of the Rosario Islands near Cartagena

attractions.text: A coral archipelago about an hour by boat from the city, with clear water, snorkelling and beach clubs.
attractions.tip: Book a boat for a full day.

attractions.name: Getsemaní
attractions.text: A colourful neighbourhood of murals, plazas, hostels and bars, centred on Plaza de la Trinidad.

attractions.name: Convent of La Popa
attractions.text: A hilltop convent with views over the city.

thingsToDoIntro: Cartagena rewards wandering, eating and a day on the water.

thingsToDo.title: Take a boat to the islands
Dance salsa
thingsToDo.text: In Café Havana or Getsemaní bars.

accommodation.intro: Stay in the old city or Getsemaní.

gettingThere.intro: Cartagena has an airport and bus links.

options.text: About 1.5 hours from Bogotá or Medellín.
About 15 minutes at a fixed fare.

bestTime.headline: December–April
bestTime.summary: Cartagena is hot year-round, with a dry season from December to April.

seasons.text: Hot and humid, with some rain.
The wettest months, with flooding possible.

tips: Go out early and in the evening.
